name: L-citrulline
short: A review of 12 small trials in postmenopausal women reported no adverse effects. A crossover trial of citrulline malate reported stomach discomfort in about 15% of participants.
text: A systematic review of 12 randomised trials (360 postmenopausal women; 4 to 8 weeks) of citrulline, given directly or as watermelon products, reported no adverse effects related to supplementation in any study. In contrast, a randomised crossover trial in 41 men of a single 8 g dose of citrulline malate (citrulline combined with malate, not L-citrulline alone) reported a feeling of stomach discomfort in 14.63% of participants as the only side effect. A review of vascular effects noted that longer-term L-citrulline supplementation lowers blood pressure, an effect evident in adults with raised blood pressure but not in those with normal blood pressure. These trials were small and short. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
